newsitem.title: FRANCE: French voters disappointed with Chirac -poll.
newsitem.headline: French voters disappointed with Chirac -poll.

text.p: An overwhelming majority of French voters are disappointed with President Jacques Chirac's performance although a growing number find him personally likeable, an opinion poll published on Tuesday showed.

The SOFRES institute poll for a group of regional newspapers, taken in late December, found that 69 percent of voters said the results of Chirac's first 19 months in office had been negative, while only 21 percent found them positive.

Only 16 percent said they were satisfied with Chirac's action in office, compared to 69 percent dissatisfied. A mere 13 percent said he had kept the promises he made as a presidential candidate, while 78 percent said he had broken them.

The poll of a representative sample of 1,000 adults showed 42 percent of French voters personally liked the president, while 32 percent said they had little liking for him and 25 percent had none at all.

Forty-one percent said he acted as the president of all the French people, compared to 53 percent who said he did not. On both these questions, Chirac had gained in support since a similar year a year earlier.
Among qualities, 30 percent found him energetic, 25 percent warm and 22 percent tolerant but only 18 percent competent and 17 percent sincere.
Among defects, 34 percent said he often changed his mind, 23 percent found him authoritarian and 20 percent superficial.
